title: Chapter 36
content:
Tae-jeong tracked Seh-hwa’s retreating back with a steady gaze. The kid was doing his absolute best, but honestly, Tae-jeong could close the gap in half a dozen strides if he stretched his legs. Still, the boy pressed on, limping with desperate urgency, occasionally casting a glance at the ceiling. He was clearly fighting with everything he had to hold back the tears.

It was baffling how much tragedy one person could carry. Crying at the drop of a hat, leaking slick at the slightest touch... Even whenever Tae-jeong caught a glimpse of those lips, they were always parted and wet.

“What a pain in the ass.”

He never should have promised to keep the kid breathing. Sacrificing everything from the knees down wouldn't interfere with carrying a pregnancy, but Tae-jeong knew damn well that the boy’s desperate plea not to be abandoned carried an unspoken condition: in one piece. Safely, all the way to the end. Clearing the threshold alone was child's play, but dragging Seh-hwa across the line was an entirely different operational headache.

Tae-jeong tapped his wrist unit against the locking ring of the Z2 casing. A standard-issue service watch was hardly just a timepiece; it served as a biometric tag, a frequency sniffer, an access pass, a comms terminal, and a tactical slate all in one—a wrist-mounted military supercomputer. With a Brigadier General’s clearance, there wasn't a single standard partition across the armed forces he couldn't override. The criminal identity he wore lacked the clearance, of course, but Park was already scrubbing that exact footage from the data stream in real time.

Click. The moment the casing popped open, Tae-jeong torqued his torso back to maximize leverage. The throwing distance was uncomfortably tight, but he had run kinetic breach drills under worse conditions dozens of times. And he had never missed.

He knew how to push every sensory organ past biological limits. How his nervous system pulled off that calibration was a mystery even to him; the command researchers who had processed him as a child had eventually grown terrified of the very monster they’d created. But that inhuman sensory control was the sole reason he was still drawing breath today.

The ambient roar in his ears dropped off sharply. Erasing his own respiratory rhythm, Tae-jeong dialed his focus entirely into the trajectory of the payload. The black sphere arced through the air, carving a clean, silent parabola down the hall.

Snatching the discarded rocket launcher in one hand, he launched into a full sprint. Watching the maneuver during live-fire exercises, Lieutenant Park had once remarked that the entire world seemed to freeze while the General moved at quadruple speed. Tae-jeong silently hoped the trick held up one more time.

He hooked a hand around the industrial shelving as he passed, dragging two heavy steel units down to choke the corridor. It was a token barricade at best, far too light to catch the full brunt of the fragmentation. How much air time left? The sphere reached the apex of its arc, decelerating just before gravity pulled it down.

He kicked his pace into overdrive. The familiar, pathetic silhouette of the oversized brown top bobbed right ahead. Tae-jeong lunged, clamping his hand around Seh-hwa’s collar like plucking a stray kitten from the gutter. The boy let out a choked gasp, thrashing clumsily in midair. Having large palms had its perks—he could secure both the unhinged Z2 lid and Seh-hwa’s neck with one arm.

The boy’s eyes went wide as he looked back over his shoulder. Yeah, definitely shouldn't have put those tinted lenses in. Right as that stray thought drifted through his head, the charge detonated.

Low-yield or not, high-explosives were high-explosives. A brutal shockwave of superheated air slammed into their backs, launching them forward.

“Aargh…!”

Seh-hwa took the worst of the spill, hitting the deck with a violent skid before he could even summon a full scream.

The saving grace was that the sphere had detonated against the falling portcullis, directing the bulk of the kinetic force backward, while the dry-chemical supplies on the racks snuffed out the worst of the ignition. Even so, hesitating for another three seconds would see them roasted alive in the expanding backdraft.

“Cough…”

Seh-hwa lay gasping, concussed from the impact. The skin across his bare feet was torn raw, and his left ankle had already swollen to the size of a baseball. Fragile little shit. What the hell am I supposed to do with this?

“The vials.”

Tae-jeong clicked his tongue and demanded the haul. Without a second of delay or backtalk, Seh-hwa yanked his oversized hem up to expose the bag. At least the kid had the survival sense to understand when the clock was ticking. Knowing the boy lacked the motor control to work the zipper, Tae-jeong tore the pocket open himself, sweeping the loaded syringes into the clear Z2 housing. He slammed the lid shut, the internal lock engaging with a sharp, heavy snap.

Pushing his sweat-drenched bangs back, Tae-jeong held the sealed casing up toward the camera dome. A rhythmic series of double-taps ticked through his earpiece. Capture confirmed.

“Almost out.”

Tae-jeong checked the receiver on the surplus launcher. The antique tube was already rattling loose from battering the steel racks earlier; it had two firings left in it at best. Forcing a third risked catastrophic misfire in his own hands. Tae-jeong popped the caps off several emergency fuel canisters resting on the lower shelves, then glanced down at Seh-hwa.

“Can you hold this? It’s not going to blow up anymore.”

The boy nodded like a vacant doll. Beneath the bubbling, half-melted edge of the prosthetic skin, streaks of black soot coated his jaw. The kid looked like an absolute disaster—a stray mutt living behind a machine shop would look more presentable. Tae-jeong clicked his tongue, oblivious to the fact that the harsh line of his own mouth had softened completely.

“No piggyback this time.”

He didn't wait for a response. Hauling Seh-hwa up by the waist like a sack of grain, he hoisted him over one shoulder and surged forward. The endless rows of industrial shelving finally cleared out around Section 9-5. Just a little farther to the breach point.

The ceiling above gave another violent lurch. The coward monitoring the security grid was making his final, desperate play. Dropping Seh-hwa onto his feet, Tae-jeong delivered a brutal roundhouse kick to the nearest support strut. The collapsing frame wedged directly into the teeth of an incoming security grate, buying a narrow window of clearance.

“Lee Seh-hwa!”

Hearing his real name snap through the smoke, the glassy daze in the boy’s eyes shattered, replaced by a flicker of focus.

Ducking beneath the collapsing iron frame that was screaming under the weight of the dropping ceiling, Seh-hwa stumbled forward blindly, dragging blood-slicked feet across the jagged concrete. He was practically crawling, but he was moving toward Tae-jeong with everything he had.

Tae-jeong could have stepped in and hauled him out. It would have been infinitely faster to drag him by the collar across the threshold. The kid’s shredded feet would scream in agony, but Seh-hwa had already made it clear he preferred pain over death.

Yet Tae-jeong couldn't pull his eyes away from the sight of the boy limping forward on his own. The iron portcullis grinding the steel racks into scrap, the deafening concussions overhead, the red tongues of flame licking through the smoke behind them… and the boy, looking at nothing else in the world except him. Tae-jeong watched the clumsy, desperate approach with a strange, unmoored gaze.

The trance broke the second his fingers snagged the canvas edge of that ridiculous brown top. Reeling the boy in with an iron grip, Tae-jeong kicked the emergency egress door wide open. The manual latch sheared under the heel of his boot, leaving just enough clearance for two bodies to squeeze through.

Behind them, the compromised steel rack buckled completely under the structural collapse, the shriek of tearing metal echoing through the dust. Seh-hwa shuddered in his arms.

“I-Is it… over?”

Clutching the contraband casing against his ribs, Seh-hwa scanned the staging area with wide, terrified eyes.

“Almost.”

The exit opened onto a staging apron currently serving as a private motor pool for the garrison. A space originally designed for rapid-deployment emergency gear had been repurposed as a private parking lot for officers’ personal vehicles.

“Fucking undisciplined clowns.”

Tae-jeong singled out a high-end luxury sports coupe parked closest to the doors—undoubtedly purchased on an astronomical installment plan by some mid-tier officer. He could practically hear the owner’s phantom weeping. Should’ve parked in designated stalls, dipshit.

Tae-jeong planted a hand on the hood to check the chassis as a triple-tap chimed through his earpiece. Evidence secured, surveillance loops fried. High command was blind; they were cleared to run hot.

He tapped his service watch against the driver’s side door sensor. Any vehicle registered under active military personnel was legally subject to emergency command commandeering, allowing the watch to force the lock. If it had been an unregistered black-market ride, hotwiring it would have burned precious seconds.

As Tae-jeong cracked the throttle and dropped the panoramic glass roof, Seh-hwa scrambled into the passenger seat, holding down the peeling edges of his rubber disguise. The central console lit up with an ostentatious holographic marque, a synthetic voice chiming cheerily to confirm autonomous transit mode.

“Hold on.”

Tae-jeong racked the heavy launcher into the cabin and slammed the driver’s side door. The long, massive weapon rested heavily against the center console, its muzzle jutting prominently through the open roof. Seh-hwa reflexively wrapped both hands around the base, terrified the swaying steel would crush him.

Annoyed by the cramped seat position adjusted for a shorter driver, Tae-jeong aggressively mashed the toggle controls. Short-legged bastard buying a car like this... The second his boot hit the accelerator, the engine roared to life, launching the chassis forward with violent torque. The raw exhaust note ripped through the open roof, slamming Seh-hwa hard against the seat before he could even secure his harness. The sudden jerk tore the loose edge of his prosthetic skin wide.

“What are you, a cat? Why do your bones have zero structure?”

Tossing out the scolding, Tae-jeong caught Seh-hwa’s wrist and guided his fingers toward the transmission tunnel.

“Harness on. When I give the word, press this button.”

Seh-hwa’s fingertip rested squarely atop a toggled switch marked S.
